focus: unaided selection of strong and thorough evidence

assigned_texts.source: Authored for Manuel Academy High School ELA; Academy-held rights.
assigned_texts.accessible_representation: Digital reflowable text, enlarged print, or audio, learner's choice.

essential_question: How does close, evidence-governed attention to unaided selection of strong and thorough evidence change what a reader or writer is entitled to claim?
learning_objectives: Explain what unaided selection of strong and thorough evidence means and reconstruct, unprompted, the criteria a strong response must meet.
Apply unaided selection of strong and thorough evidence to an unfamiliar text without an exemplar, working at the high end of the grades 9-10 text complexity band, independently and proficiently.
Judge whether the learner's own evidence is sufficient, and revise where it is not.
success_criteria: The response meets criteria the learner stated from memory, with no exemplar consulted.
The evidence offered is sufficient for the claim, not merely consistent with it.
The learner identifies and repairs the weakest link in their own reasoning.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
the unit's assigned texts, in an accessible reading representation
citation reference or style manual appropriate to the course

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a short retrieval prompt on unaided selection of strong and thorough evidence. Ask the learner to predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.

Ask the learner to attempt unaided selection of strong and thorough evidence cold, before any instruction. Record what they already do well. Nothing here is scored, and errors here are data, not failure.
Name what the diagnostic revealed in neutral, non-character language. State the unit question and what will count as evidence by the end of it.

Walk the unit's destination: Lead an evidence seminar on a self-selected band-level text and submit an analytical evidence dossier.. The learner writes down what they think will be hardest about it and why. The tutor may question this prediction but may not write it.
The learner records one specific thing about unaided selection of strong and thorough evidence they intend to be able to do by the end of the unit.

student_activity: Attempt unaided selection of strong and thorough evidence without instruction, then record a personal goal for the unit.
formative_check: Name one thing about unaided selection of strong and thorough evidence you can already do and one you cannot do yet.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid readings when the evidence supports them. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for unaided selection of strong and thorough evidence, re-teach it on a short passage, then retry one fresh item. Do not write the learner's response.
Ask the learner to explain why the move for unaided selection of strong and thorough evidence works on this text before continuing. Accept explanation in any modality.
Name specifically what the reasoning got right about unaided selection of strong and thorough evidence, offer one varied case, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Describe the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a correct case, and schedule a short later review of unaided selection of strong and thorough evidence.
Decline to supply the assessed response. Offer a question, a criterion, or a counterexample instead, and record that guided support was given.

Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate unaided application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one at the high end of the 9-10 band with no exemplar available.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate unaided application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one at the high end of the 9-10 band with no exemplar available.
extension: Apply the move to an unfamiliar text at the high end of the band with no exemplar and no checklist.
student_authorship: The learner writes every assessed response. The tutor may explain, question, critique, or suggest a revision direction.
The tutor must not draft, rewrite, or supply sentences for an assessed response, and must not complete a graded task on the learner's behalf.
Tutor assistance is logged as guided evidence; unaided work is logged as independent evidence. Mastery requires independent evidence.
Fixed-form assessment items keep their answer key adult-only; the key is never surfaced in a learner-facing surface.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and make the success criteria visible in text.
Allow typed, handwritten, dictated, or recorded-to-text responses; the response mode is not the standard.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, transcripts, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Provide an accessible reading representation (digital reflowable text, enlarged print, or audio) for every assigned text.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about writing and reading difficulty.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Offer an alternate text or private response when content is personally sensitive.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; fictionalized or analytical alternatives are always acceptable.
Presentation may be delivered privately to the facilitator; no public or recorded performance is ever required.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, annotated passage, recorded reading, or short clip supporting unaided selection of strong and thorough evidence.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable text, alt text, or a transcript. No media is required to meet the standard.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw drafts, raw private reflections, recordings, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one real-world instance of unaided selection of strong and thorough evidence in something they already read. No purchase, account creation, or private disclosure is required.
performance_task_link: Lead an evidence seminar on a self-selected band-level text and submit an analytical evidence dossier.

essential_question: How does close, evidence-governed attention to parallel structure sustained across long passages change what a reader or writer is entitled to claim?
learning_objectives: Explain what parallel structure sustained across long passages means and reconstruct, unprompted, the criteria a strong response must meet.
Apply parallel structure sustained across long passages to an unfamiliar text without an exemplar, working at the high end of the grades 9-10 text complexity band, independently and proficiently.
Judge whether the learner's own evidence is sufficient, and revise where it is not.
success_criteria: The response meets criteria the learner stated from memory, with no exemplar consulted.
The evidence offered is sufficient for the claim, not merely consistent with it.
The learner identifies and repairs the weakest link in their own reasoning.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
the unit's assigned texts, in an accessible reading representation
citation reference or style manual appropriate to the course

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a short retrieval prompt on parallel structure sustained across long passages. Ask the learner to predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.
State one question about parallel structure sustained across long passages the reading must answer. The learner writes the question in their own words before reading.

Uninterrupted reading and annotation of the assigned text, working at the high end of the grades 9-10 text complexity band, independently and proficiently. No instruction interrupts this block. An accessible reading representation is used if preferred.
The learner extracts the passages bearing on parallel structure sustained across long passages, records why each was selected, and marks the one they are least sure about.
In one concise response, state the most important claim about parallel structure sustained across long passages and one check that would expose a weak or unsupported reading.

student_activity: Read the assigned text sustained and uninterrupted, then harvest and justify the evidence bearing on parallel structure sustained across long passages.
formative_check: Quote the single passage that most changes your reading of parallel structure sustained across long passages, and say what it changes.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid readings when the evidence supports them. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for parallel structure sustained across long passages, re-teach it on a short passage, then retry one fresh item. Do not write the learner's response.
Ask the learner to explain why the move for parallel structure sustained across long passages works on this text before continuing. Accept explanation in any modality.
Name specifically what the reasoning got right about parallel structure sustained across long passages, offer one varied case, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Describe the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a correct case, and schedule a short later review of parallel structure sustained across long passages.
Decline to supply the assessed response. Offer a question, a criterion, or a counterexample instead, and record that guided support was given.

Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate unaided application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one at the high end of the 9-10 band with no exemplar available.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate unaided application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one at the high end of the 9-10 band with no exemplar available.
extension: Apply the move to an unfamiliar text at the high end of the band with no exemplar and no checklist.
student_authorship: The learner writes every assessed response. The tutor may explain, question, critique, or suggest a revision direction.
The tutor must not draft, rewrite, or supply sentences for an assessed response, and must not complete a graded task on the learner's behalf.
Tutor assistance is logged as guided evidence; unaided work is logged as independent evidence. Mastery requires independent evidence.
Fixed-form assessment items keep their answer key adult-only; the key is never surfaced in a learner-facing surface.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and make the success criteria visible in text.
Allow typed, handwritten, dictated, or recorded-to-text responses; the response mode is not the standard.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, transcripts, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Provide an accessible reading representation (digital reflowable text, enlarged print, or audio) for every assigned text.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about writing and reading difficulty.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Offer an alternate text or private response when content is personally sensitive.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; fictionalized or analytical alternatives are always acceptable.
Presentation may be delivered privately to the facilitator; no public or recorded performance is ever required.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, annotated passage, recorded reading, or short clip supporting parallel structure sustained across long passages.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable text, alt text, or a transcript. No media is required to meet the standard.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw drafts, raw private reflections, recordings, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one real-world instance of parallel structure sustained across long passages in something they already read. No purchase, account creation, or private disclosure is required.
performance_task_link: Produce a style-manual-conformant edited manuscript with a documented editorial rationale for each change.
